text:
Maria: Heads-up — starting ~04:00 UTC we saw sporadic gRPC failures (~0.5% of requests) from GPU nodes in pool-gamma. Prometheus shows short retransmit spikes on east-west flows. Anyone watching the overlays?
AJ: got the alert. first spike at 04:02. looks localized to az-eu2a rack.
Leo: can you paste a pcap or if possible tcpdump? I ran `ss -s` on a box and noticed retransmits on 10.244.x.x->10.244.y.y flows.
Maria: attaching quick snippets: 
````
# from gpu-worker-03
$ ip -s link show vxlan0
1701: vxlan0: <BROADCAST,MULTICAST,UP,LOWER_UP> mtu 1450 qdisc noqueue state UNKNOWN
    RX: bytes  123456789 packets 12345 errors 0 dropped 7 overruns 0 frame 0
    TX: bytes 987654321 packets 54321 errors 0 dropped 0 overruns 0 carrier 0
```
`dmesg` on that host has repeated: `mlx5_core: Warning: mlx5: CQE error on SQ` — not sure if related.
Julie: dropped RX on vxlan0 is suspicious. VXLAN/Geneve overhead + GSO/GRO differences often cause weird fragmentation/checksum problems.
DevOps Bot: [deploy-bot] rolling restart of kube-proxy in pool-gamma scheduled at 05:00 UTC.
AJ: quick `ping -s 1400 -M do` between two affected nodes shows intermittent fragmentation fails, and latency spikes ~20-50ms for short windows.
Leo: I ran `iperf3 -u -b 1G` — UDP microbursts look fine. TCP tests show occasional window stalls and duplicate ACKs on inner TCP. Suspect PMTU or offload mismatch with encapsulation + RDMA offloads.
Maria: config notes: we run Geneve overlay, host NIC MTU=9000, vxlan/geneve devices set to 1450. Some nodes still have `ethtool -K ib0 gso on gro on lro on` from driver defaults.
NetOps: NICs? Mellanox/driver/firmware details?
Leo: mlx5_core driver, firmware 5.95, driver build 5.3.0. Fleet is mixed: some nodes on kernel 6.1, others on 5.15 (we started a rolling kernel upgrade last week).
Julie: kernel/driver skew is a big hint. Newer kernels changed how offloads are handled for encapsulated packets.
AJ: captured tcpdump on gpu-worker-07 during a spike: many UDP-encap packets retransmitted; inner TCP shows duplicate ACKs and retransmits.
Maria: host qdisc during spike:
````
qdisc mq on eth0
qdisc fq_codel 8002: dev vxlan0
# rtt stats show bursts ~60ms
```
DevOps: any correlation with autoscaler/backfill churn?
Maria: yes — spikes align with scheduled backfills that moved ~50-100 pods between 03:55-04:05. That churn increases tunnel endpoint churn (lots of new encapsulation states).
Leo: working hypothesis: during heavy pod migrations the kernel offloads (GRO/LRO) produce large offloaded frames; encapsulation then truncates or invalidates checksums and the NIC/driver reports errors, exposing inner TCP retransmits. Kernel + firmware mismatches amplify it.
Julie: quick reproduce steps to validate:
- repro cluster with two nodes and RDMA offloads enabled
- run `sysctl -w net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`
- toggle `ethtool -K ib0 gro off gso off lro off` and observe

AJ: applied a canary mitigation: disabled GRO/GSO on `ib0` on 3/20 GPU nodes. In the canary window retransmits dropped to near zero.
Maria: exact commands used for the canary:
````
for n in gpu-canary-01 gpu-canary-02 gpu-canary-03; do ssh $n "sudo ethtool -K ib0 gro off gso off lro off"; done
kubectl annotate node gpu-canary-01 infra.offload=disabled
```
NetOps: disabling offloads is heavy but it reduced errors. What about perf impact?
Leo: perf test shows CPU for GRPC traffic up ~4-6% per node with GSO off; acceptable as a short-term mitigation. Latency smoothed out.
DevOps: longer-term options: align kernel + firmware across pool, driver patch from vendor, or lower overlay MTU and enable PMTU probing cluster-wide.
Julie: filed internal ticket IT-4521 to coordinate kernel alignment for the GPU fleet and raised vendor case VENDOR-786 for the CQE warnings.
Maria: added a node-exporter metric for `vxlan0_dropped` and a short alert so we get earlier warnings next time.
AJ: also throttled backfill/autoscaler burst: reduced simultaneous pod moves from 100 -> 10 and added jitter. Patch: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/1234
Leo: tested `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=2` on a canary — improved behavior for PMTU changes when tunnels rehome. Recommend enabling cluster-wide after validation.
Timeline summary: 
- 04:00 detect
- 04:15 canary offload-disable -> retransmits dropped
- 04:40 backfill throttle rolled
- 05:10 vendor ticket + IT ticket created

AJ: proposal: roll out offload-disable to all GPU nodes for a rolling 24h window while we validate kernel alignment. Any objections?
Julie: fine but stagger the change and watch CPU + GRPC tail latencies.
NetOps: I'll schedule a maintenance window and include NIC firmware coordination if vendor asks.
Maria: I'll keep posting traces. If you see `CQE error on SQ` on any node please @me with node name and recent dmesg.
SRE Bot: alert cleared for pool-gamma at 05:25 UTC — retransmit counters normalized.
Leo: postmortem TODOs: confirm root cause (offload+encap+kernel skew), short-term remediation (offload disable + backfill limits), long-term (driver/firmware fix, MTU policy, kernel alignment). Follow-ups: IT-4521, VENDOR-786.
Maria: will create a short incident note and copy actionable commands into the GPU-network runbook. Closing updates unless new spikes appear.
